description: College students, working on developing, learning and exploring anything that sounds interesting!
summary: We developed ARES-IV, an advanced interactive web application designed for Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route planning, surface traversal, and risk assessment across Gale Crater and the boxwork sulfate formations of Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp) on Mars. The application addresses the critical challenge of high-risk Martian terrain navigation by combining regional DEMs with local slope and hazard modeling, allowing mission planners and simulated astronauts to plot optimal, safety-gated paths while avoiding steep scarps ($>18^\circ$), loose regolith traps, and life-support budget overruns. This project is vital because it bridges the gap between macro-scale orbital observations and micro-scale astronaut safety, ensuring reliable, data-backed mission execution on the Martian surface.
details:
• What it does & How it works: ARES-IV features a dual-view architecture consisting of a 2D Terrain Traversal View for waypoint placement and adaptive $A^*$ pathfinding, and an interactive 3D Globe powered by Three.js with raycasting and surface layer changes. It queries live surface telemetry from NASA feeds and evaluates slope grades, life-support duration, and thermal constraints in real-time.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: It provides precise mission planning capabilities, reduces surface operational risks, and empowers users to evaluate traversability across hazardous Martian formations. The intended impact is to advance analog planetary exploration tools and improve surface operational safety for future crewed and robotic missions.
  • Tools, Languages & Software: Developed using HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript, leveraging Three.js for 3D rendering and orbital visualization.
  • Creativity & Considerations: The project uniquely integrates real-time NASA MSL meteorological telemetry with multi-scale planetary map visualization, balancing strict physiological and mechanical EVA constraints (such as suited speed and slope hazard thresholds) with intuitive aerospace HUD styling.
